method: PHRF time-on-distance corrected time is the elapsed time in seconds minus the rating in seconds per nautical mile multiplied by the course distance in nautical miles, so a 120 s/nm boat over 10 nm receives a 1,200 s (20:00.0) allowance. Portsmouth Yardstick time-on-time corrected time is the elapsed time multiplied by 1000 and divided by the boat's number, so one hour at 950 corrects to 1:03:09.5 and at 1250 to 48:00.0. The time allowance is the corrected time subtracted from the elapsed time: positive values are time credited to the boat and negative values are time it gives away. Corrected and elapsed pace divide those times by the course distance, and speeds are the distance in nautical miles divided by the time in hours. The elapsed time accepts m:ss, h:mm:ss or plain seconds with at most one decimal place and must fall between 10 s and 24 hours; the PHRF rating must be from -300 to 600 s/nm, the Portsmouth number from 500 to 1600, and the course distance from 0.1 to 1000 nm with up to two decimals. Under PHRF a combination that credits more time than was sailed is rejected because the corrected time would be negative. Ratings are class lookups and are not derived here, the distance is the rated course length rather than a GPS track, and current, wind, crew weight, start penalties and rating appeals are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
